title: NIST AI RMF — Four Functions
blurb: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage. Sort each activity into the function it belongs to.
source: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 (AI 100-1), January 2023
hint: Drag each activity onto its function. Govern runs across all of them; Map establishes context, Measure quantifies, Manage acts.
note: Govern is not a phase that finishes. If an activity sets the conditions under which the other three happen — culture, accountability, policy — it is Govern, whenever it occurs.

zones.name: Govern
zones.def: Cultivate a culture of risk management: policies, accountability structures, roles, workforce capability, third-party oversight. Cuts across the other three.

zones.name: Map
zones.def: Establish context and frame risks: purpose, setting, actors, impacted people, capabilities and limitations, interdependencies.

zones.name: Measure
zones.def: Analyse, assess, benchmark and monitor using quantitative and qualitative methods, including the trustworthiness characteristics.

zones.name: Manage
zones.def: Allocate resources to mapped and measured risks: prioritise, respond, recover, communicate, and act on third-party and residual risk.

items.label: The organisation documents who is accountable for AI risk decisions and at what level each class of decision may be taken.
items.why: Accountability structures are the archetypal GOVERN activity. Without them the other three functions have no one to report to and no one to escalate to.

items.label: An AI policy is approved, aligned to legal requirements, and its exceptions process is defined.
items.why: Policy and its exception route set the conditions under which every other activity happens. GOVERN is cross-cutting, not sequential.

items.label: Staff working on AI systems are given role-specific training and their competence is tracked.
items.why: Workforce capability sits squarely in GOVERN. A measurement regime nobody is competent to run produces numbers without assurance.

items.label: Processes are established for overseeing third-party models and data, including what must be obtained from suppliers.
items.why: GOVERN explicitly covers third-party oversight policy. Applying it to a specific vendor's risk on a specific system is MANAGE.

items.label: The team documents the system's intended purpose, deployment setting, and the categories of people it will affect.
items.why: Framing context is the whole point of MAP. Skipping it is how a system is later measured accurately against the wrong objective.

items.label: Known capabilities, limitations and assumptions of the system are catalogued, including where it should not be used.
items.why: MAP establishes what the system is and is not for. The out-of-scope statement authored here is what later evaluation and monitoring are judged against.

items.label: Internal and external stakeholders, including affected communities, are identified along with the benefits and potential harms to each.
items.why: Identifying impacted parties and framing potential impacts is MAP. Quantifying those impacts is MEASURE.

items.label: Interdependencies with other systems and the consequences of the AI component failing are traced.
items.why: MAP covers the system in its wider context, including what else breaks when it does. A component viewed in isolation is a mapped risk missed.

items.label: The system is benchmarked against defined metrics for validity, reliability and robustness before release.
items.why: MEASURE covers assessment against the trustworthiness characteristics using repeatable methods.

items.label: Performance is evaluated separately for each demographic subgroup and the disparity is quantified.
items.why: Analysing harmful bias with quantitative methods is MEASURE. Deciding what to do about the disparity is MANAGE.

items.label: Ongoing monitoring instruments the deployed system for input drift and quality degradation.
items.why: MEASURE includes continuous monitoring after deployment, not only pre-release testing. Drift detection lives here.

items.label: Test, evaluation, verification and validation methods are chosen, documented, and their own limitations recorded.
items.why: MEASURE requires that the measurement approach itself be assessed. A metric with unexamined blind spots is a false assurance.

items.label: Risks are prioritised against impact and resources are allocated to the highest first.
items.why: Prioritisation and resource allocation across mapped and measured risks is the definition of MANAGE.

items.label: A response plan is put in place covering incident containment, recovery and communication for a model failure.
items.why: MANAGE covers responding to, recovering from and communicating about incidents. Writing the plan is MANAGE; rehearsing capability is GOVERN.

items.label: Residual risk after mitigation is documented and communicated to the deployer of the system.
items.why: MANAGE explicitly addresses residual risk, including telling downstream users what remains. Undocumented residual risk is transferred by accident.

items.label: A decision is taken to decommission a deployed model whose risk can no longer be brought within tolerance.
items.why: Superseding or decommissioning a system is a MANAGE response. Having a defined route to retirement is what makes it possible.
